text: {"components": [{"type": "claim", "quote": "The energy label for bathroom products indicates whether shower heads, fittings and water-saving attachments are energy-efficient by classifying them in categories from A (high level of efficiency) to G (low level of efficiency).", "gist": "Bathroom product energy labels classify efficiency from A (most efficient) to G (least efficient)"}, {"type": "claim", "quote": "The aim with this label is to increase people's awareness of the need to use hot water more sparingly.", "gist": "The label aims to raise awareness about conserving hot water"}, {"type": "claim", "quote": "This benefits the environment and also reduces costs.", "gist": "Saving hot water helps the environment and lowers expenses"}, {"type": "claim", "quote": "The production of hot water requires a great deal of energy – in a modern house or apartment, often more than is required for room heating.", "gist": "Heating water uses a lot of energy, often more than heating rooms"}, {"type": "entity", "quote": "Swiss Association for Energy-Efficient Sanitary Products SVES", "gist": "SVES is the Swiss association for energy-efficient sanitary products"}]}
